questiontext.text: Which problem statement is most useful to begin a troubleshooting investigation?

answer.text: At 10:15 the course page timed out on one VM; the desktop remained responsive
The computer is broken
Linux is always unreliable
The network must be hacked

questiontext.text: What should generally happen before making a system change during troubleshooting?

answer.text: Define the symptom, scope it, and collect relevant evidence
Delete old logs and restart every service
Change several settings at once
Assume the newest change caused the problem

questiontext.text: Which is an observation rather than an inference?

answer.text: systemctl status reports that the unit is failed
The group owner must be wrong
The update caused the failure
The hardware is defective

questiontext.text: The most recent system change is always the cause of a problem that appeared afterward.

answer.text: true
false

questiontext.text: Why test one variable at a time?

answer.text: It helps connect a changed result to the tested condition
It guarantees there is only one cause
It removes the need to document results
It makes every command run as root

questiontext.text: What does systemctl status UNIT --no-pager provide?

answer.text: Human-readable runtime status and recent log information without opening a pager
It restarts the unit and clears its logs
It edits the unit file
It lists only files installed by the unit

questiontext.text: What does systemctl is-failed UNIT check?

answer.text: Whether the named unit is in the failed state
Whether all system files are damaged
Whether the unit is enabled at boot
Whether the unit's package can be removed

questiontext.text: What does journalctl -u UNIT -n 30 --no-pager request?

answer.text: Up to 30 recent journal entries for the unit without opening a pager
It deletes the unit's 30 oldest journal entries
It starts the unit and follows its output forever
It prints all user passwords associated with the unit

questiontext.text: In journalctl --since "1 hour ago" -p warning, what does -p warning select?

answer.text: Warning-priority messages and more severe priorities
Only messages created by the warning application
Messages exactly one hour old
Only successful service starts

questiontext.text: If a journal query shows no matching entry, the event definitely did not occur.

answer.text: true
false

questiontext.text: What does df -h report?

answer.text: Filesystem capacity and usage in human-readable units
Directory permissions only
Installed package sizes only
Network interface capacity

questiontext.text: What does du -h --max-depth=1 PATH summarize?

answer.text: Space used by immediate subdirectories under PATH in human-readable units
Free memory on the system
Disk health and remaining device lifetime
Every file's permissions below the entire root filesystem

questiontext.text: Why might an investigator run date --iso-8601=seconds?

answer.text: To record the current time in a standardized format for the timeline
To change the system clock to a new time
To sort journal entries by severity
To show filesystem capacity

questiontext.text: What information does uptime help provide?

answer.text: System uptime and load averages
Disk space used by each directory
Package source signatures
Routes to remote networks

questiontext.text: Why is high “used” memory in free -h not automatically evidence of memory exhaustion?

answer.text: Linux uses available memory for caches, so available memory and swap context matter
The command always reports disk space instead
Memory use cannot affect performance
All used memory belongs to inactive users

questiontext.text: What does ip address display?

answer.text: Current interfaces and assigned network addresses
Only DNS server logs
Firewall policy and open services
Systemd unit state

questiontext.text: What does ip route display?

answer.text: Current routing entries, possibly including a default route
Every process using the network
Firewall rules on every router
Which hostnames are valid on the Internet

questiontext.text: A configured default route proves that the system has working Internet access.

answer.text: true
false

questiontext.text: What does getent hosts NAME query?

answer.text: The system's configured host name-resolution path
The local firewall's list of allowed ports
Whether a systemd unit is failed
Whether the filesystem is full

questiontext.text: A bounded ping to the gateway receives replies. What does this establish?

answer.text: The tested ICMP exchange with that gateway succeeded at that time
Every Internet service is working
Name resolution is working for every host
All firewall rules are correct

questiontext.text: What does ps aux provide during an investigation?

answer.text: A snapshot of process information
A list of every installed package's signature
A continuously updating resource display
A backup of process memory

questiontext.text: A process should be terminated immediately whenever it appears near the top of a CPU-use list.

answer.text: true
false

questiontext.text: Why should log excerpts be redacted before sharing?

answer.text: Logs may include usernames, addresses, paths, request data, or secrets
Redaction makes timestamps more accurate
Logs cannot be understood unless every line is removed
All logs are public information

questiontext.text: Why should an investigator inspect context after filtering log output with grep?

answer.text: Filtering may hide nearby entries needed to understand a message
grep changes system configuration
Filtered output always contains false messages
It disables logging for the service

questiontext.text: Which information is most useful in a troubleshooting handoff?

answer.text: Impact, timeline, expected/actual behavior, evidence, tests, results, and next action
Only an unsupported guess at the root cause
All logs including credentials and unrelated user data
A list of commands with no outputs or explanation

questiontext.text: After an authorized repair, repeat the original task under comparable conditions to verify the result.

answer.text: true
false

questiontext.text: When is escalation especially appropriate?

answer.text: When a change could affect shared systems, security, availability, or data, or evidence suggests compromise
Whenever a command returns any output
Only after deleting logs
Never; every user should independently fix production systems

questiontext.text: In the lab case, / is 99% used while /home has substantial free space. Which conclusion is best supported?

answer.text: The root filesystem appears constrained; the next step is to identify usage there without deleting files
All data on /home should be deleted
The network route is broken
The service should be restarted immediately

questiontext.text: A service log says “Permission denied” while opening a database path. What should the student conclude?

answer.text: It supports an access-related hypothesis, but path, ownership, permissions, and configuration still need checking
The correct fix is to make every file world-writable
The kernel must be defective
The message proves that the service is malicious

questiontext.text: How does top differ from ps aux in the lesson?

answer.text: top provides a changing, interactive process view; ps aux is a snapshot
top edits process files, while ps aux edits logs
They both terminate the highest CPU process automatically
ps aux continuously changes network routes

questiontext.text: What does head do when used to sample command output?

answer.text: Shows the beginning portion of the input; context may still need review
Deletes old log entries
Changes a service's ownership
Displays only network routes
